- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#5 ("Outline rev 3 vs PROTOCOL.md: secondary n/N, per-target bias draws, ceiling check, source-count analysis") by `experiment-repo`  > R = 100 per-target bias is done (`scripts/14_bias_r100.py`; files `results/highR/` (03_analyze output), `results/highR_vs_main.csv`, `results/highR_target_bias.csv`, log `results/logs/highR_vs_main.txt`; raw `results/raw_highR/`, not in git).
  > 
  > **Covers:** interp and extrap splits only (no lineage, no anchor design, no cat), n = 100, designs uniform/strat/pps/balanced, 10 folds-worth of targets as in the main run (3203 interp / 799 extrap targets, 13 non-thin benchmarks), R = 100 subset draws per fold (draws 0–9 equal the main run's).
  > 
  > **Does Table 3 change? No, at the table's reading.** Mean over benchmarks of bias²_unbiased / var / MSE, each over the MSE of uniform×mean, R = 10 → R = 100 (SE over benchmarks of the R = 100 bias² in brackets):
  > - uniform×IRT model: interp bias² 0.32 → 0.33 (0.08), var 0.37 → 0.36; extrap bias² 4.29 → 4.42 (0.84), var 0.27 → 0.27, MSE 4.56 → 4.69.
  > - uniform×diff. IRT: interp 0.07 → 0.07, var 0.46 → 0.45; extrap 0.23 → 0.24 (0.06), var 0.52 → 0.53.
  > - balanced×diff. IRT: interp 0.08 → 0.08; extrap 0.27 → 0.27. PPS×diff. IRT: 0.06 → 0.07; 0.28 → 0.28.
  > - uniform×cal. reg.: interp 0.06 → 0.06; extrap 0.58 → 0.59. balanced×mean: 0.03 → 0.02; 0.09 → 0.09. strat×mean: 0.00 → 0.00; uniform×mean: −0.01 → 0.00 (interp; the R = 10 negative value is its estimation noise).
  > Largest change over the 10 table rows available in both runs is +0.13 (uniform×IRT model, extrapolation), 3 % of that cell and ≈ 0.15 of its SE across benchmarks; everything else ≤ 0.02. The bias²_unbiased correction at R = 10 therefore works (it agrees with R = 100 within noise); the conclusion "the IRT model's extrapolation error is 94 % squared bias" stands (R = 100: share of squared error that is bias² = 0.94 pooled over targets). Not covered by R = 100: the lineage columns and the anchor×IRT plug-in row of Table 3 (they stay at R = 10, `bias2_unbiased`).
  > 
  > **Per-target view (pooled over targets, R = 100):** per-target Monte-Carlo SE of the draw-mean bias is median 0.002–0.004 (score units, i.e. 0.2–0.4 points). Extrap: uniform×IRT model median |bias| 0.060, |bias| > 2 SE in 99.6 % of targets; uniform×ridge model 0.041, 99.0 %; uniform×cal. reg. 0.033, 96.6 %; uniform×diff. IRT 0.019, 85 %; balanced×diff. IRT 0.016, 82 %; uniform×mean 0.003, 7.4 % (about the 5 % expected under no bias). Interp: IRT model 0.010 (79 %), diff. IRT 0.006 (57 %), cal. reg. 0.006 (59 %), uniform×mean 0.003 (3.8 %). So the difference estimators' remaining bias is detectable in most targets but small (0.6–1.9 points against a 0.2–0.3 point MC SE); that bias is 18–20 % (interp) and 47–48 % (extrap) of their squared error.
